windows.fallback: falls back to a native ProfileList registry enumeration (no login count) when the Security channel is inaccessible
requires an elevated token to read the Security channel; reports an error otherwise

caveats: **`session_history`'s Linux/macOS fields do not line up with the declared schema.** The Windows leg (`users_win_events.hpp:329-333`) fills `event_type|logon_type|source|timestamp|detail` correctly, but the Linux/macOS leg (`users_plugin.cpp:1279-1305`, `:1328-1352`) does a raw `ls >> user >> tty >> source` against `last`'s columns and writes `(tty, source-token, derived-console/remote/system, completed/active/crash, free-text-remainder)` into those same five slots. The real timestamp only exists as unparsed free text inside `detail`. Do not consume this action's Linux/macOS output as if it matched the Windows/YAML field semantics.

**`sessions`' idle time is always `0` on Windows.** The code queries `WTSSessionInfo` but never decodes the returned `IdleTime`, explicitly "for simplicity" (`users_plugin.cpp:511-525`). Linux/macOS idle text (via `w`) is real.

**Windows-only exclusion filter.** `primary_user`/`session_history`'s Windows leg drops machine accounts (`...$`) and `SYSTEM` (`users_win_events.hpp:236-237`); the Linux/macOS `last`-based leg instead drops `reboot`/`shutdown`/`wtmp` boilerplate lines. A description that says "excludes machine accounts and SYSTEM" without an OS qualifier is describing the Windows leg only.

**`local_users`' Linux last-logon lookup is gated by `is_safe_identifier`.** A username outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` (most commonly an AD/Samba machine account ending `$`) skips the `lastlog -u` call and reports `last_logon=unknown`; the account row is still emitted (`users_plugin.cpp:590-606`).

**A minimal Linux image can be missing `lastlog`/`last` entirely.** The 2026-09-06 container capture had neither on `$PATH`: `local_users` degraded to `unknown` last-logons and `UNAVAILABLE`, and `primary_user`/`session_history` failed outright with the same status — while `logged_on` (utmp), `local_admins`/`group_members` (native `getgrnam`), and `sessions` (`w`, which was present) were unaffected. The same capture's `group_members group=sudo` returned zero rows and no `error` row: `getgrnam` only emits `group_member|error|Group not found: <name>` and returns 1 when the group doesn't exist (`users_plugin.cpp:971-975`); zero rows with rc 0 means the `sudo` group existed but had no explicit members and no `/etc/passwd` account with a matching primary GID (`users_plugin.cpp:976-1008`).

definitions.description: Lists members of a specified local group. On Windows queries NetLocalGroupGetMembers and reports member type (user, group, well_known_group, alias). On Linux reads /etc/group and checks primary GID assignments in /etc/passwd. On macOS reads the group via dscl. The group name is a required parameter.

Lists members of the local Administrators group. On Windows this queries the Administrators group via NetLocalGroupGetMembers and reports member type (user, group, well_known_group, alias) and domain. On Linux checks sudo/wheel groups plus root. On macOS reads the admin group via dscl.

Enumerates local user accounts on the endpoint. Reports the username, enabled/disabled status, last logon timestamp, and account description. On Linux reads /etc/passwd (skipping system accounts with UID < 1000), on macOS uses dscl, on Windows uses NetUserEnum. On macOS, also reports console_state — a tri-state ("true"/"false"/"unknown") signal for whether the account is the current GUI/console-login user; Linux and Windows omit this field entirely rather than leaving it empty. On Linux, a username containing characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] skips the lastlog lookup and reports last_logon as "unknown".

Enumerates currently logged-on users on the endpoint. Reports each user's name, domain/host, logon type (console, RDP, remote), and session identifier. Uses WTS APIs on Windows, utmp on Linux, and the 'who' command on macOS.

Identifies the primary user of the endpoint by analyzing login frequency. On Windows queries Security Event Log for Event ID 4624 (logon) events and counts occurrences per user, falling back to the registry profile list when the Security channel is unreadable. On Linux and macOS parses the output of the 'last' command instead, capped at the 200 most recent lines. Returns the user with the most login events and the count. On Windows, machine accounts (ending with $) and SYSTEM are excluded from the Security Event Log count; on Linux/macOS, 'last' boilerplate lines (reboot, shutdown, wtmp) are excluded instead.

Shows historical login and logout session records. On Windows queries the Security Event Log for Event IDs 4624 (logon) and 4634 (logoff), parsing logon type, source address, and timestamps. On Linux and macOS parses the 'last' command output instead — the six output fields are populated positionally from 'last', not from the same event-log semantics as Windows: the "event_type" field carries the tty, "logon_type" carries last's host/source token, "source" carries the derived console/remote/system classification, "timestamp" carries the completed/active/crash status, and the real date/time lives in "detail" as free text. The count parameter controls how many records to return (clamped to 1-500). Requires elevated privileges on Windows to read the Security event log.

Lists active interactive sessions on the endpoint, including session state (Active, Connected, Disconnected, Idle), the connected user, remote client name or host, and idle time. Uses WTS session APIs on Windows and the 'w' command on Linux/macOS. The idle field is always "0" on Windows — idle-time decoding is not implemented there.

description: Reports logged-on users, sessions, local accounts, admin group members, group membership, primary user, and session history
how_it_works: All seven actions are reads (`Mutability::None` on every leg); nothing in this plugin creates, deletes, or modifies an account, session, or group. `logged_on`/`sessions` answer "who is on this box right now" from the OS's live session table (utmp, WTS, or `who`/`w`). `local_users`/`local_admins`/`group_members` enumerate account and group membership from the OS's own directory (passwd/group, Directory Services, or the Windows Net APIs) — `group_members` takes an arbitrary group name as a parameter, `local_admins` is a fixed lookup of the built-in admin group. `primary_user` and `session_history` both mine login history — the Security event log on Windows, `last` on Linux/macOS — the former reducing it to one answer (the most-frequent account), the latter returning it as time-ordered rows. On Linux/macOS every OS-tool invocation goes through a bounded, no-shell argv runner (`run_tool`, ADR-3002 rung 2) with a 10s deadline; a tool that fails to spawn, times out, or is killed reports itself through the ABI4 result-status seam rather than surfacing as a silent empty list.

inputs.description: Name of the local group to enumerate members for (e.g., "Administrators", "Remote Desktop Users", "sudo").
inputs.name: group

inputs.description: Maximum number of session records to return, as a digit string (e.g. "100"); values outside 1-500 are clamped back to the default of 50.
inputs.name: count

name: users

columns.name: member_name

columns.description: The kind of membership. Values: user, primary_group (Linux only); Windows: user, group, well_known_group, alias.
columns.name: member_type

columns.description: The name of an account or group belonging to the local admin membership. Values: free text.
columns.name: member_name

columns.description: The kind of member. Values: user (always on Linux/macOS); Windows: user, group, well_known_group, alias, unknown.
columns.name: member_type

columns.description: The domain owning the member (Windows), or the source group/account name (Linux "sudo"/"wheel"/"root", macOS literal "admin"). Values: free text.
columns.name: domain_or_group

columns.description: The local account's username. Values: free text.
columns.name: username

columns.description: Whether the account is enabled. Values: true, false.

columns.name: last_logon

columns.description: The account's comment/description text (Windows comment, macOS RealName, Linux GECOS field), or "-" when empty. Values: free text or "-".
columns.example: Built-in account for administering the computer/domain
columns.name: description

columns.description: Tri-state flag for whether this account is the current GUI/console-login user; the field is entirely absent (not empty) on Linux and Windows. Values: true, false, unknown.
columns.name: console_state

columns.description: The account name of a currently logged-on user. Values: free text.
columns.name: username

columns.description: The host or domain the session belongs to, or the literal "local" when it has none. Values: hostname/domain or the literal "local".
columns.name: domain

columns.name: logon_type

columns.description: The session's terminal identifier — a utmp line name (Linux), a tty (macOS), or a numeric WTS session ID (Windows). Values: free text.
columns.name: session_id

columns.description: The account with the most login events in the examined history, or "unknown" when none could be determined. Values: free text or "unknown".
columns.name: username

columns.description: The number of login events counted for this user; "0" for the Windows ProfileList fallback, which carries no count. Values: integer.
columns.name: login_count

columns.description: How the answer was derived. Values: last (Linux/macOS); event_log_4624, profile_list (Windows); free text on a query failure.
columns.name: source

columns.description: The account named in the record. Values: free text.
columns.name: username

columns.description: Windows: "logon" or "logoff". Linux/macOS: actually the session's tty, not an event-type label — see the plugin README's Caveats. Values: logon, logoff (Windows); a tty name (Linux/macOS).
columns.name: event_type

columns.description: Windows: the mapped LogonType name or raw numeric code, empty when absent. Linux/macOS: actually last's host/source token, usually empty for a local session. Values: interactive, network, batch, service, unlock, network_cleartext, new_credentials, remote_interactive, cached_interactive, or a raw numeric code (Windows); free text, often empty (Linux/macOS).
columns.name: logon_type

columns.description: Windows: the event's IpAddress, or "-". Linux/macOS: actually the derived console/remote/system classification, not a network source. Values: an IP address or "-" (Windows); console, remote, system (Linux/macOS).
columns.name: source

columns.description: Windows: the event's TimeCreated, full-precision UTC. Linux/macOS: actually the completed/active/crash status word, not a timestamp — the real date/time is embedded in "detail". Values: ISO-8601 UTC (Windows); completed, active, crash (Linux/macOS).
columns.name: timestamp

columns.description: Windows: the raw EventID text. Linux/macOS: the remainder of the 'last' line verbatim (weekday, date, time, and logout/duration or "still logged in"). Values: free text.
columns.name: detail

columns.description: The session's controlling tty (Linux/macOS) or numeric WTS session ID (Windows). Values: free text.
columns.name: session_id

columns.description: The account that owns this session. Values: free text.
columns.name: username

columns.description: The session's connection state. Values: Active (Linux/macOS, always); Windows: Active, Connected, Disconnected, Idle, Listen, Other.
columns.name: state

columns.description: The remote host the session connects from ('w' FROM column) or the RDP client name on Windows; "-" when none. Values: free text or "-".
columns.name: client

columns.description: Idle time as reported by 'w' on Linux/macOS; always the literal "0" on Windows, where idle-time decoding is unimplemented. Values: free text (Linux/macOS) or the literal "0" (Windows).
columns.name: idle

outputs_note: Pipe-delimited rows, one per record, discriminated by a literal first field (`user`, `session`, `local_user`, `admin`, `group_member`, `primary_user`, or `session_history`). Unlike some collector plugins, `logged_on`/`sessions`/`group_members` emit **zero rows**, not a placeholder, when there is nothing to report (an empty Windows/Linux `logged_on` and `sessions` capture is exactly this case — see Sample output) — the empty result is legitimate on its own and is not itself a failure signal; only the typed result status (below) tells a genuinely degraded read apart from a clean empty one. A query-level problem (missing/invalid parameter, tool not found, group not found) instead emits a single `<action>|error|<message>` row. `local_users` additionally varies its own field count by OS: Linux and Windows rows carry 4 data fields, macOS rows carry 5 (`console_state` is appended, not padded in with a placeholder) — `users_plugin.cpp:800-806`.

privileges.grant: **None** for the other six actions (WTS/NetAPI calls succeed under the daemon's own account). `session_history` (and `primary_user`'s Security-log path) needs an elevated token to read the Security channel — an unelevated read reports `PERMISSION_DENIED`/`CONSTRAINED`/`UNAVAILABLE` depending on the failure (`users_plugin.cpp:234-253`) and `primary_user` still answers via the ProfileList fallback.
privileges.if_refused: `session_history`/`primary_user` set a typed result status (see Result status below) and emit an `error`-prefixed row naming the cause

privileges.grant: **None.** Every leg is either an IOKit-free `dscl`/`who`/`w`/`last` argv call or the shared `SCDynamicStoreCopyConsoleUser` console-user read — no elevated open.
privileges.if_refused: a spawn/timeout is forwarded via `forward_runner_failure` as `UNAVAILABLE`/`CONSTRAINED`; the action falls back to its own "unknown"/error row text

privileges.grant: **None** for the native legs (utmp, `getgrnam`, `getpwuid`). `local_users`/`primary_user`/`session_history` also shell out to `lastlog`/`last`, which need to be present on `$PATH` — the 2026-09-06 container capture had neither installed, and both actions degraded to `UNAVAILABLE`/`PARTIAL`.
privileges.if_refused: a missing/failed tool is forwarded via `forward_runner_failure` as `UNAVAILABLE`/`CONSTRAINED`; native legs (`logged_on`, `local_admins`, `group_members`) are unaffected

result_status.when: default; every OS tool/native call `exited` (any exit code) — this is the status on every clean or intentionally-empty read, e.g. every sample's `logged_on`/`sessions`
a POSIX `run_tool()` call hits its `max_lines` cap (`primary_user`'s 200-line bound) before the tool finished — deliberate truncation, not a failure
a POSIX tool exceeds the 10s `kUsersCmdDeadline` or is killed/signalled mid-run
`probe_tool_path` found no binary, or the spawn itself failed — the 2026-09-06 Linux container sample (`lastlog`/`last` missing)
Windows Security-channel query denied (`session_history`, `primary_user`'s event-log path)

rows: local_user|Administrator|false|2021-10-14 11:15:58|Built-in account for administering the computer/domain
local_user|DefaultAccount|false|Never|A user account managed by the system.

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result only.** Rows travel the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the `ResponseStore` (90-day default retention, `server/core/src/response_store.hpp:153`), queryable at `/api/responses/{id}`.

**Not consumed by** daily-sync inventory, the TAR warehouse, DEX, or metrics — nothing in this plugin runs on a schedule; `gather.ttlSeconds` (60–300s per definition) is a repeat-query cache TTL, not a cron trigger.

**Sensitivity.** Every action's rows name a specific account: `username`/`member_name` (local or logged-on account names, including admin-group members), `domain`/`domain_or_group` (Windows domain or hostname), and `session_history`'s Windows leg carries the raw Security-log event detail for that account's logons/logoffs. `session_id`/`client` can carry a remote hostname or RDP client name — a device identifier for whatever machine connected in. No column carries installed-software data.

**Siblings:** `core.crossplatform.users` (`content/definitions/users_set.yaml`, "User Account Management") is the mutating counterpart in a separate plugin — this plugin never creates, deletes, disables, or reassigns an account.

**MCP / REST.** Discover: `discover_plugins` (summary) → `yuzu://plugin-docs` (this page as data) → `discover_instructions` / `get_definition("device.users.session_history")`. Run: `execute_instruction {definition_id, parameters}`. Read: `/api/responses/{id}`.
